text:
maria: Noticed repeated small-gpu pod rebinds in ap-se1 after scheduler routed off ap-se1a. Anyone else seeing this?
tim: Yep. attach latency spikes (~300-700ms) on a subset of nodes caused scheduler to mark them Unavailable -> fallback to ap-se1b. ap-se1b hit packing pressure and we saw affinity evictions.
sre-bot: Alert: conntrack-near-capacity on ap-se1a nodes (driver=eni-v3). Fallback policy engaged.
ops-lead: Quick mitigation: bump scheduler attach threshold to 400ms for ap-se1 and reserve 2 GPUs per AZ for tiny-ephemeral lane. Can we canary?
maria: Canaries live at 5% traffic. I'll open the canary config PR and watch eviction-rate metric.
tim: I'll patch a daemonset sysctl to increase conntrack headroom on the affected nodes. Rolling to 25% now.
maria: Early canary shows reduced rebinds. Adding follow-ups: RFC for "lane_affinity" label and a daily conntrack drain check job. Postmortem to follow. :thumbsup:
